name: Documents: Climate Litigation Database export
task: The documents: filings, pages, extracted text. Every citation comes from here.
source: Sabin Center for Climate Change Law (Columbia Law School) with Climate Policy Radar; use authorised by Maria Antonia Tigre (Sabin Center)
note: 16,791 filings, 569,218 indexed pages. Text extracted with OCR where needed.

name: Name search, first version
task: Finds the citations (the name of the case in all its forms) and extracts page and passage. The rows and the passage shown come from here.
status: replaced by S02 for the rows that name the case (29 September 2026); the July semantic search is paused since 27 September 2026
note: Name forms are in the case files (74 for Urgenda). Urgenda rows from the run of 3 September, Neubauer and Future Generations from 23 September. Two defects, corrected in S02: the semantic filters (reranker threshold, decision date) also applied to rows that name the case and were found by both networks; long references were split into two rows. Code: `cerca.py` as it was on 28 September 2026, the last version before the S02 corrections; the runs of 3 and 23 September may have used an earlier revision.
hardware: Apple M5 Pro, macOS 27.0 (the research group's Mac)

name: Name search, corrected
task: Finds the citations that name the case. No semantic filter on rows that name the case; an identifier (docket number, ECLI, web address) close to the previous match continues the same citation; Korean and Japanese forms of Urgenda.
status: in use: rows added and rows merged in the platform

measures.name: rows merged (one citation split in two rows)
rows already judged, found again by the new search

note: Merged rows stay in the database marked as merged, with the row they were merged into. Added rows did not carry machine readings until the rereading of 30 September.
hardware: Apple M5 Pro, macOS 27.0 (the research group's Mac)

name: Citation reading, first version
task: As L02, without the rule on footnotes. Two readings per row, on every citation of Urgenda.
status: replaced by L02 (its readings are kept in the archive)
note: Replaced because the external reader and the coders disagreed mostly in footnotes (agreement 0.32 in footnotes against 0.60 in the body). The code of this first reading was not kept apart: it is `classifica_lessicali.py` before the footnote rule (L02).
hardware: NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (ReCaS-Bari data centre, INFN and University of Bari)

name: Choice of the nearby pages to read
task: On top of the T01 scores: a page up to 10 pages before or after the citation enters the uptake reading if its highest score on a principle is at least 0.5 (from 2 pages before to 3 after) or 0.8 (further away); at most 5 pages per citation.

measures.name: threshold 0.8 for the far pages
measures.value: measured: on the pages read 4 to 10 pages from the citation, above 0.8 more than half are real continuation

measures.name: threshold 0.5 for the near pages
measures.value: not measured: inherited from the previous system, to be calibrated on the team's judgments

note: A rule, not a model: calibrating it does not retrain T01. If T01 is retrained, the thresholds are recalibrated. The codebook 0.3-pilot (dimension 7) still writes the window {before: 2, after: 3}: it will say 10 in the next version of the codebook, not in the file registered for L02 and L03, whose fingerprint is not touched.
hardware: Apple M5 Pro, macOS 27.0 (the research group's Mac)

name: Paragraph map

name: Uptake reading with the case dossier: continuation, quotes, supported sentence

status: in use since the evening of 29 September 2026 for the continuation, the quotations and the supported sentence (window up to 10 pages, R03). Not for the principles, since 30 September: it decides on the footnote sentence alone and does worse than L04 against the principal investigator's judgments (§63.35)
hardware: NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (ReCaS-Bari data centre, INFN and University of Bari)
note: Instructions of the evening of 28 September 2026; readings run on 29 September 2026. The footnote rule comes from a case flagged by the principal investigator: brief to the Inter-American Court, p. 51 and p. 54 (Klimaatzaak at footnote 205).
what_changes: same model; the instructions add the case dossier, the footnote rule, the verbatim quotation and the supported sentence

name: TRACE-Reranker 0.1
task: Scores a principle against a text (citation passage, nearby pages): proposes principles and nearby pages to read.

training.settings: LoRA rank 16 on q,k,v,o; 2 epochs; three seeds averaged; «uptake» instruction; 2,560 tokens

hardware: NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (ReCaS-Bari data centre, INFN and University of Bari)

AUC on the 133 semantic test rows
measures.value: 0.787: NOT a measure of implicit uptake (§63.24)

family: TRACE model trained by the project

name: Rules that put the proposals together
task: Puts together R01, the readings L02-L05 and L07 and the T01 scores into the proposals the team sees, with the codebook rules.
rules: ticked principles: those from the paragraph map (R01) and from the reading (L04 since 30 September; L05 before); the reranker (T01) is a hint and never ticks
chain mention: principle «none»; hints remain visible
no continuation page is ticked when the citation takes no principle
the sentence under a nearby page is shown as a quotation only if it is found verbatim in the page
since 30 September 2026: a page ticked on a principle the row does not propose stays listed, it is not removed
note: Writes only on rows without a human judgment. Open defect (review of 30 September 2026, point 2): principles written by the reader without the case prefix are silently dropped when compared with the ids of the case file; the prefix correction exists only for the continuation pages.
hardware: Apple M5 Pro, macOS 27.0 (the research group's Mac)
